newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks mixed, close 0.07pct up on weak banks.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks mixed, close 0.07pct up on weak banks.

text.p: Greek stocks were mixed on Tuesday as mild profit-taking in banks which lead this year's rally was more than offset by strong performance in industrials and construction.

The Athens general index opened higher and hit an intraday high of 1,529.97, up 0.76 percent, before profit-taking pushed it lower to close at 1,519.48 points, up 0.07 percent or 1.06 points higher on the day.
Banks finished 0.39 percent lower and industrials were led 0.80 percent higher mostly by bouyant cement and metallurgical stocks.
Construction enjoyed a long-awaited, brisk recovery due to increased buying interest, edging 4.04 percent ahead. Small-caps also finished 3.99 percent higher.
Analysts said profit-taking following sizeable recent gains was inevitable and desirable.

"Caution should be shown because the conditions which characterised the February 1997 downturn are here again. Banks came to a halt while other sectors advanced on momentum," said Aris Faliagas, analyst at Avax Securities.
Time might be ripe for a mild, 50-point correction in the absence of panic-selling as the market prepares for the new round of appreciation towards the historic high of 1,680, he added.
Profit-taking in banks was viewed favourably because it alleviated price imbalances among different sectors and offered investors new opportunities for gains.
"Transfer of funds from banks to industrial and construction stocks improve conditions for a broadly-based rally," said Faliagas.
Constructions have lagged behind and we are reaching completion of the five-year cycle typical of the Greek textile sector in which high gains are realised, he added.
Turnover continued to rise, amounting to 25.2 billion drachmas in total volume of 7.7 million shares.
Blocks were traded in Petzetakis, 259,000 shares at 1,365 drachmas, Hellenic Bottling, 40,000 shares at around 8,950, and Alpha Credit, 15,000 shares at 20,100 drachmas.
Advancing stocks beat decliners 150 to 85 with 18 stocks unchanged on 253 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 1,107.0-1,137.0. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were down 45 drachmas at 6,550.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $68.61-$70.31. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 2,646-2,851 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $15.67-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
